body.statement: Under the balanced rank-one one-block L-mask assumptions, there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(\alpha\), \(\mu\), \(\kappa\), \(s_-\), and \(s_+\), such that for all sufficiently large even \(n\), \[c\sigma\sqrt n\le\rho_{\alpha,n}^{\star}\le C\sigma\sqrt n.\] The upper bound is attained by the total polynomial-time one-block procedure \(\mathsf{WSVD}_n\), whose conditional Gaussian, finite-simulation, homogeneous Taylor, and fallback contributions are each \(O(\sigma\sqrt n)\). The lower bound holds for every procedure uniformly honest over all tuples \(\vartheta_n\in\Theta_n\).
body.justification: The benchmark distinguishes collective low-rank uncertainty from the order-\(n\) radius obtained by summing entrywise intervals.
body.gap: Yan and Wainwright prove sharp scalar widths, and Capponi and Stojnic characterize Frobenius residuals of one algorithm; neither gives an all-procedure tuple-indexed honest nuclear-radius frontier.
body.consumer: Researchers can report a simultaneous uncertainty set for the entire treated counterfactual block at a sub-diameter scale.
